% Shared Tikz Preamble for Diagram Atomization Pipeline
% Load this in every tikz generated by Phase 5 subagents.
% Do NOT redefine these — use exactly this preamble.

\documentclass[tikz,border=2pt]{standalone}

% Core libraries
\usetikzlibrary{
    arrows.meta,       % arrow styles
    positioning,       % relative placement
    cd,                % commutative diagrams (tikz-cd)
    calc,              % coordinate calculations
    shapes.geometric,  % ellipses, polygons, etc.
    shapes.misc,       % rounded rectangles, etc.
    decorations.markings,  % arrow on paths
    backgrounds,       % background layer
    fit,               % fitting nodes around others
}

% Standard arrow tip
\tikzset{>=Stealth}

% Commutative diagram style
\tikzcdset{
    arrows={>=Stealth},
    row sep/normal=3em,
    column sep/normal=4em,
}

% Common node styles
\tikzset{
    mathnode/.style={rectangle, draw=none, fill=none, inner sep=2pt},
    labelnode/.style={rectangle, draw=none, fill=none, font=\small, inner sep=1pt},
}

\begin{document}
%
% Serre spectral sequence diagram
% Fibration: ΩS⁴ → PS⁴ → S⁴ (path-loop fibration)
% Homological E² = E⁴ page with d₄ differentials
% Only columns p=0 and p=4 are populated (H_*(S⁴) ≅ ℤ at degrees 0,4)
%

\begin{tikzpicture}
  % Grid matrix: 6 rows (q=5..0) × 6 columns (p=0..5)
  \matrix (m) [
    matrix of math nodes,
    nodes in empty cells,
    row sep=2.5em,
    column sep=3em,
    nodes={font=\small, inner sep=2pt}
  ] {
    % Row 1: q = 5 (top of grid)
    H_{5}(\Omega S^{4}) & {} & {} & {} & H_{5}(\Omega S^{4}) & {} \\
    % Row 2: q = 4
    H_{4}(\Omega S^{4}) & {} & {} & {} & H_{4}(\Omega S^{4}) & {} \\
    % Row 3: q = 3
    H_{3}(\Omega S^{4}) & {} & {} & {} & H_{3}(\Omega S^{4}) & {} \\
    % Row 4: q = 2
    H_{2}(\Omega S^{4}) & {} & {} & {} & H_{2}(\Omega S^{4}) & {} \\
    % Row 5: q = 1
    H_{1}(\Omega S^{4}) & {} & {} & {} & H_{1}(\Omega S^{4}) & {} \\
    % Row 6: q = 0 (bottom of grid)
    H_{0}(\Omega S^{4}) & {} & {} & {} & H_{0}(\Omega S^{4}) & {} \\
  };

  % q-axis labels (vertical / fiber degree) — placed to the left of each row
  \node[labelnode, left=0.6em of m-1-1] {5};
  \node[labelnode, left=0.6em of m-2-1] {4};
  \node[labelnode, left=0.6em of m-3-1] {3};
  \node[labelnode, left=0.6em of m-4-1] {2};
  \node[labelnode, left=0.6em of m-5-1] {1};
  \node[labelnode, left=0.6em of m-6-1] {0};

  % p-axis labels (horizontal / base degree) — placed below the bottom row
  \node[labelnode, below=0.6em of m-6-1] {0};
  \node[labelnode, below=0.6em of m-6-2] {1};
  \node[labelnode, below=0.6em of m-6-3] {2};
  \node[labelnode, below=0.6em of m-6-4] {3};
  \node[labelnode, below=0.6em of m-6-5] {4};
  \node[labelnode, below=0.6em of m-6-6] {5};

  % d₄ differentials — three that land on visible grid cells
  %   d₄: (4,0) → (0,3): from column 5, row 6 to column 1, row 3
  \draw[->] (m-6-5) -- (m-3-1);
  %   d₄: (4,1) → (0,4): from column 5, row 5 to column 1, row 2
  \draw[->] (m-5-5) -- (m-2-1);
  %   d₄: (4,2) → (0,5): from column 5, row 4 to column 1, row 1
  \draw[->] (m-4-5) -- (m-1-1);

  % d₄ differentials — three that extend beyond the visible grid (q > 5)
  %   These have the same bidegree (−4, +3) but target q = 6, 7, 8.
  %   We draw the shaft and clip the arrowhead at the diagram boundary.
  %   (4,3) → (0,6): from column 5, row 3, going (−4,+3) in grid coords
  \draw[->, shorten >=1.5em] (m-3-5) -- ($(m-3-5)+(-12em,-7.5em)$);
  %   (4,4) → (0,7)
  \draw[->, shorten >=1.5em] (m-2-5) -- ($(m-2-5)+(-12em,-7.5em)$);
  %   (4,5) → (0,8)
  \draw[->, shorten >=1.5em] (m-1-5) -- ($(m-1-5)+(-12em,-7.5em)$);

\end{tikzpicture}
%
\end{document}
